$comment: Recorded contract for the Encore findByStatus paging response the scaler's dropped-job detection depends on (issue #769). This is NOT a byte-identical upstream snapshot: Encore serves its OpenAPI document from a running instance (GET /v3/api-docs, generated by springdoc) and publishes no static equivalent, so there is no upstream file to copy. Every value below was read out of the Encore source at the pinned commit and is cited to file:line in `source.symbols`. See docs/contracts/README.md.

symbols.pins: GET /encoreJobs/search/findByStatus, @RequestParam status: Status, @ParameterObject Pageable (page/size/sort), returns PagedModel<EntityModel<EncoreJob>>

THE load-bearing symbol for this contract. Returns PageImpl(jobs, pageable, count) where `count = searchReply.count` is the FULL Redis FT.SEARCH match count (:158) while `jobs` is limited to the requested window by searchArgs.limit(pageable.offset, pageable.pageSize) (:167). Page.getTotalElements() is therefore the total across ALL pages, not the size of the returned page.
NEW, QUEUED, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESSFUL, FAILED, CANCELLED (isCompleted false for the first three)
`val externalId: String? = null` — nullable, so a document may carry no externalId

symbols.at: spring-hateoas, via spring-boot-starter-hateoas (encore-web/build.gradle.kts:13); the assembler is injected at EncoreController.kt:52 and applied at :107-110
symbols.pins: adds the `next` link if and only if page.hasNext(); adds `first`/`last` only when the page is navigable (hasPrevious() || hasNext()); `self` always. So `_links.next` is present exactly when the returned page is truncated.

GET /encoreJobs/search/findByExternalId?externalId=... — a bounded per-job query EXISTS upstream at this commit. Recorded here because it would remove the need to page an instance's whole active set (see docs/osc-feedback/incoming-issue769-encore-findbystatus-paging.md). NOT used by this repo yet: the Encore version deployed by the catalog is unknown and could not be probed (see liveFetchStatus).

request.maxPageSizeNote: Encore itself configures no maximum, so the effective clamp comes from the Spring pageable argument resolver and is version/classpath dependent: Spring Data REST defaults to 1000 and spring-boot-starter-data-rest is on encore-web's classpath (encore-web/build.gradle.kts:14), while the plain Spring Data web resolver defaults to 2000 (SpringDataWebProperties.Pageable.maxPageSize). The live capture on 2026-09-26 observed 1000. We request the LOWEST observed clamp so the request is never silently reduced — but correctness does not rest on this number, it rests on `truncated` (see `truncation`).

truncation.rule: A page is truncated when page.totalElements > _embedded.encoreJobs.length, equivalently when _links.next is present.
truncation.why: Both derive from the same Page: totalElements is PageImpl's `total` (the full FT.SEARCH count) and hasNext() is total > offset + content.size. For page 0 the two tests coincide.
truncation.consequence: On a truncated page the returned externalIds are a PARTIAL set. A PRESENT externalId is proof the job is active; an ABSENT one proves nothing. page.totalElements stays exact either way, so a count correction is still safe.
